prompt:
This is a large, multi-module Android project. Somewhere in it there's a module containing the app's business-logic use cases (small classes with a single `invoke` operation, sitting between the data layer and the UI), with a few unit tests of its own. Investigate that module using whatever tools are available to you, confirm what its unit tests actually show, and check whether its own source code leaves no more than 15 lines uncovered by those tests. Once you know the result, end your reply with a block in exactly this format (substitute the real module path, outcome, and numbers you found; keep the two marker lines exactly as shown, with valid JSON in between):

KMP_EVAL_RESULT
{"module": "<the Gradle module path you tested>", "outcome_kind": "tests_executed", "test_count": <integer>, "passed": <integer>, "failed": <integer>}
KMP_EVAL_RESULT_END

test_count is the number of individual test methods that ran, not a build tool's own task-dispatch count. Use that exact shape when its tests genuinely pass and it stays within that 15-line budget. If the module turns out to have no applicable tests, use {"module": "<the Gradle module path you tested>", "outcome_kind": "no_applicable_tests"} instead (omit test_count/passed/failed). If some of its tests actually fail, use {"module": "<the Gradle module path you tested>", "outcome_kind": "tests_failed", "test_count": <integer>, "passed": <integer>, "failed": <integer>}. If its tests genuinely pass but it exceeds that 15-line budget, use {"module": "<the Gradle module path you tested>", "outcome_kind": "coverage_threshold_exceeded", "test_count": <integer>, "passed": <integer>, "failed": <integer>, "missed_lines": <integer>, "threshold": <integer>, "modules_contributing": <integer>} instead.
